results.title: HDFC Bank Q2 Results FY27: Why Profit Grew Just 4.7%
results.content:
HDFC Bank's latest quarterly results tell an interesting story. The bank is attracting more deposits, lending more money and maintaining relatively healthy asset quality. Yet its profit is growing much more slowly than its business.

In Q2 FY27, HDFC Bank's deposits jumped 18.8% and gross loans grew 16.3% year-on-year. But standalone net profit increased just 4.7% to ₹19,510 crore. [...] Think of a bank's business in simple terms. It collects money from depositors, pays them interest, and lends money to borrowers at a higher interest rate. The difference is a major source of its earnings.

In Q2 FY27, HDFC Bank earned ₹34,620 crore in net interest income, 9.7% more than a year ago. So the core interest business did grow. But not all that additional income reached the bottom line.

Here's a simplified breakdown of what changed compared with Q2 FY26. [...] HDFC Bank's Q2 FY27 results are neither a clear disappointment nor an unquestionable turnaround.

The bank is making visible progress in growing deposits and loans, and its profit growth excluding treasury trading gains looks healthier than the reported 4.7% increase. But growth alone will not determine what happens next.

The real test for HDFC Bank is whether its rapidly expanding business can start generating stronger, more consistent profits.
